passage.title: Raising the Mary Rose
paras: On 19 July 1545, King Henry VIII stood on the shore near Portsmouth and watched his favourite warship sail out to fight a French fleet. Suddenly, the Mary Rose leaned over, water rushed in through her open gunports, and she sank in minutes. Hundreds of men were lost.
For more than four hundred years, the ship lay on the seabed, slowly covered by silt. The silt protected one side of her hull from the creatures and currents that destroy wood.

In the 1960s, a diver named Alexander McKee began searching for the wreck. In 1971 his team found her timbers. For eleven years, divers worked in cold, murky water, recording and lifting thousands of objects: longbows and arrows, cooking pots, combs, shoes and even a dog's skeleton.

Then, on 11 October 1982, came the most difficult task of all. A huge lifting frame raised what was left of the hull from the seabed. Millions of people watched on television as the old ship rose into the air.

Wood that has been underwater for centuries crumbles if it dries too quickly. For years the hull was sprayed with water, then with a special wax-like chemical, before it was slowly dried. Today the Mary Rose can be seen in a museum in Portsmouth, close to where she sank, together with the belongings of the people who sailed in her.

questions.q: In which year did the Mary Rose sink?
How did the water get in?
What covered the ship on the seabed?

questions.a: It protected one side of the hull from creatures and currents

questions.q: Who began searching for the wreck?
Name three objects the divers lifted.
questions.a: Any three: longbows, arrows, cooking pots, combs, shoes, a dog's skeleton

questions.q: Why was the hull sprayed with water?
questions.a: Old wet wood crumbles if it dries too quickly

questions.q: Find a word that means 'dark and hard to see through'.
Why do you think millions of people watched on television?
questions.a: It was a rare, historic and difficult event to see a 400-year-old ship rise

questions.q: How does the writer show that the divers' work was hard?
Why is it fitting that the museum is in Portsmouth?
questions.a: It is close to where she sank and where she sailed from

questions.q: Summarise the passage in one sentence.
questions.a: Henry VIII's warship the Mary Rose sank in 1545, was found and raised in 1982, and is now in a museum in Portsmouth.
